ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a circle representing a great circle of the Earth, and inside the circle there is a vertical straight line passing through the center position and extending to the lower end of the circle. The three points O, A, and B are on this vertical line; O is above and is marked near the center inside the circle, A is below O, B is near the lower-end boundary of the circle, and A is between O and B. Then reason: The stem says point A is the intersection point of any two meridian circles, so A can be regarded as a geographic pole; in the figure A is in the Southern Hemisphere direction, so take A as the South Pole. B is the tangent point between the great-circle arc of the Earth and the 52°S latitude circle, and the O→A→B direction passes through the South Pole; combined with the relationship that the distance from the great-circle boundary to the center of the circle corresponds to 90°, it can be obtained that the latitude of point O is 38°S. In the date condition, the dates on the east and west sides of point B are different and the global ranges of the new and old dates are equal, indicating that the date boundary line makes the new and old dates each occupy half of the globe. According to the method draft, take the meridian where B is located as 0°; after crossing the South Pole, the meridian opposite to it is 180°, so the longitude of point O is 180°. Therefore point O is roughly located near 38°S, 180°, and the country where it is located is New Zealand. New Zealand is near the boundary between the Pacific Plate and the Indian Ocean Plate, and is mainly not a plate growth (rifting) boundary, so the incorrect statement regarding the country where point O is located is "located at a plate growth boundary".

method.method_draft: First describe the image: O, A, B are collinear on the central vertical line, A is between O and the lower boundary point B. From the text, take A as a pole and B as the tangency point with 52°S. Because the circle boundary is 90° from centre O and the route O→A→B crosses the South Pole, compute O’s latitude as 38°S. Use the date clue: when B’s east-west sides have different dates and global old/new date areas are equal, B’s meridian is 0°; crossing the pole gives O’s longitude as 180°. Identify O’s country as New Zealand, then judge the proposed descriptions of New Zealand; the incorrect one is that it is located at a plate growth/divergent boundary.

先描述图像：图中是一个表示地球大圆的圆，圆内有一条竖直的直线通过圆心位置并延伸到圆的下端。O、A、B三点在这条竖直线上，O在上方且标在圆内中心附近，A在O的下方，B在圆的下端边界附近，A位于O与B之间。
再推理：题干说A点为任意两个经线圈的交点，因此A可看作地极；图中A在南半球方向，故取A为南极。B是地球大圆弧与52°S纬线圈的切点，沿O→A→B方向经过南极；结合大圆边界距圆心对应90°的关系，可得O点纬度为38°S。日期条件中，B点东西两侧日期不同且全球新旧日期范围相等，说明日期分界线使新旧日期各占全球一半，按方法草案取B所在经线为0°；越过南极后与其相对的经线为180°，所以O点经度为180°。因此O点大致位于38°S、180°附近，所在国家为新西兰。新西兰处在太平洋板块与印度洋板块交界附近，主要不是板块生长（张裂）边界，所以关于O点所在国家不正确的表述是“位于板块的生长边界”。

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The following figure is a great circle of the Earth, point O is the center of the circle, point A is the intersection point of any two meridian circles, and point B is the tangent point between the great-circle arc of the Earth and the 52°S latitude circle. When the dates on the east and west sides of point B are different, the global ranges of the new and old dates are equal. Read the figure and answer:

<image1>

Regarding the country where point O is located, the incorrect statement is: ______.
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer: located at a plate growth boundary
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_standard_answer: located at a plate growth boundary
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The following figure is a great circle of the Earth, point O is the center of the circle, point A is the intersection point of any two meridian circles, and point B is the tangent point between the great-circle arc of the Earth and the 52°S latitude circle. When the dates on the east and west sides of point B are different, the global ranges of the new and old dates are equal. Read the figure and answer: <image1> Regarding the country where point O is located, the incorrect statement is: ______.
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: located at a plate growth boundary
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: The figure is a circle representing a great circle of the Earth, and inside the circle there is a vertical straight line passing through the center position and extending to the lower end of the circle. The three points O, A, and B are on this vertical line; O is above and is marked near the center inside the circle, A is below O, B is near the lower-end boundary of the circle, and A is between O and B.
Then reason: The stem says point A is the intersection point of any two meridian circles, so A can be regarded as a geographic pole; in the figure A is in the Southern Hemisphere direction, so take A as the South Pole. B is the tangent point between the great-circle arc of the Earth and the 52°S latitude circle, and the O→A→B direction passes through the South Pole; combined with the relationship that the distance from the great-circle boundary to the center of the circle corresponds to 90°, it can be obtained that the latitude of point O is 38°S. In the date condition, the dates on the east and west sides of point B are different and the global ranges of the new and old dates are equal, indicating that the date boundary line makes the new and old dates each occupy half of the globe. According to the method draft, take the meridian where B is located as 0°; after crossing the South Pole, the meridian opposite to it is 180°, so the longitude of point O is 180°. Therefore point O is roughly located near 38°S, 180°, and the country where it is located is New Zealand. New Zealand is near the boundary between the Pacific Plate and the Indian Ocean Plate, and is mainly not a plate growth (rifting) boundary, so the incorrect statement regarding the country where point O is located is "located at a plate growth boundary".
